title: Ha*Ash Announces No Me Hablen de Amor Tour 2027: Here Are All the Dates
summary: Sisters Hanna & Ashley will visit 18 cities in the U.S. and Canada, starting April 20 in Toronto.
contentText:
Ha*Ash is gearing up to hit the road again with No Me Hablen de Amor – Gira 2027, a tour spanning 18 cities across the U.S. and Canada. The trek kicks off on April 20 in Toronto, Billboard can announce exclusively on Monday (Sept. 21).

Promoted by Live Nation, the new tour from the popular duo made up of sisters Hanna and Ashley will stop in cities such as Chicago, Los Angeles, Phoenix, Las Vegas, Houston and New York, among others, before wrapping up on May 22 in Miami.

Related

Ha*Ash Captivates With Latin Pop-Country Performance at Billboard Latin Women in Music 2025

The Weeknd Debuts New Song Sampling 'Neon Genesis Evangelion' Theme in Japan

It follows their 2024-25 HAASHVILLE tour, which sold over 66,000 tickets and featured 16 sold-out shows across the U.S. and Canada, according to a press release from Live Nation.

“After everything we experienced with HAASHVILLE, we couldn’t wait to be back with our fans,” Ha*Ash said in a statement. “This tour represents a new chapter for us, with new songs, plenty of stories and, of course, all those songs we’ve been singing together for so many years.”

“It’s called No Me Hablen de Amor… although you already know we’ll probably end up talking, and singing about love all night long,” they added.

Tickets for the new tour will be available through a Citi presale starting Tuesday (Sept. 22) at 10 a.m. local time. For more details, click here . The general sale begins on Friday (Sept. 25) at 10 a.m. local time on the Live Nation website .

The announcement comes during a new creative phase for Hanna and Ashley. This year, the duo released the singles “Si Me Hubieras Llamado Ayer” and “¿Qué Le Pongo?”, exploring different sides of heartbreak, from learning to let go and start anew to the emotions that surface when someone from the past unexpectedly returns.

In 2025, Ha*Ash received the Unbreakable Award at the Billboard Latin Women in Music ceremony, celebrating two decades of artistic career as a sister duo that may now be more relevant than ever.
